comments.anchor: Status, and where this standard lives
comments.text: Version-traceability question (AI-assisted implementation review): could the next draft publish a dated normative snapshot mapping Google Doc Sections 3–7 to the version-qualified GitHub requirement IDs, with explicit supersession and comment-cutoff dates? Comparing the frozen GitHub commits b8fb012 and 54a7bc6 found all 127 requirement texts and levels unchanged, while this document uses a different section structure. A reviewer needs to identify the precise clause set behind a claim without treating discussion comments or WG-INPUT NEEDED items as adopted requirements. Interest: TitleChain/M5 implementation work; no conformance claim.
comments.verification: Google Docs displayed the posted comment and Comment created after submission. No normative body text was edited.

comments.text: Proposed informative asset-transfer test (AI-assisted implementation review): distinguish authority over an electronic record from authority to change the underlying deed, lease, securityholder interest or credit-retirement state. Bind the action to the exact right, instrument version, appointed capacity and authoritative system of record. Test a valid signer who lacks appointment; lease-only authority used for a deed transfer; and a locally accepted instruction rejected or unresolved in the authoritative registry. Preserve those outcomes separately from payment settlement or a successful hash check. This would exercise Identity, Authorization and Provenance together without prescribing a vendor or deciding legal title. Interest: TitleChain/M5 implementation work; no conformance claim.
